callouts.html: What justifies the use of band ratio as our fluorometry metric?

Inner filter effect: at high concentration the sample absorbs much of the excitation light before it reaches the detected volume (and re-absorbs emission), so signal stops scaling with concentration. The literature reports it from about 5 µM. Here the I(400)/I(peak) ratio stays roughly constant at 2–4 µM, then climbs from 8 µM up.

slides.q: Does adding the tet groups change the protein’s local conformation?

points.text: Asp133 sits in the rare left-handed α basin: WT +57, +16
Unclicked 2× Tet2-Et pushes it to +74, +2, about 17.5° out of its basin

slides.title: sfGFP: backbone rigidity (RMSF)
slides.q: Does the spring deform the scaffold? Does the fold stay intact?

items.cap: Cα RMSF, aligned on the barrel core
Axial force clamp between the two Cβ atoms

points.text: The β-barrel stays uniformly rigid (≈ 0.4 Å on the strands) in every system
RMSF traces of WT, 2× Tet2-Et and the springs overlie each other; only loops and tethers move
Force clamp: 0–20 pN moves the sites by hundredths of an Å; κ > 107 kBT nm⁻²
On the clicked topology κ ≈ 350 kBT nm⁻², 2–3.5× Zocchi’s generic 100: a 4 pN spring moves the sites 0.03 Å
Answer: the scaffold is not deformed; structural integrity persists

slides.title: sfGFP: forces applied, force field vs model
slides.q: How much force reaches the protein, and do the models agree with the force field?

items.cap: Force measured on the bare duplex, restraint windows
Site displacement against modelled force

points.text: Measured directly: 27 bp 28.0 pN, 40 bp 15.8 pN, 40 bp nicked 13.2 pN
That is ≈ the Euler buckling load (27 bp: 26.8 pN); up to 35 pN in the largest box
Zocchi’s kinked branch predicts only 2.4–6.6 pN: the force field gives ≈ 6× more
Every construct pulls its sites slightly together; displacement vs force r = +0.08, p = 0.81 over 11 constructs
Even the force-free 50 nt ssDNA loop compresses the sites by 0.32 Å, as much as any duplex

slides.title: sfGFP: DNA dynamics
slides.q: Is the DNA kinked or coiled? Does it interact with the protein beyond pushing?

items.cap: Axis bend per base-pair step along each duplex
Base-pair opening against imposed curvature

points.text: The duplex bends smoothly at 4.8–5.2°/bp, nucleosome-like, with no local spike
Only 0.03–0.83 base pairs open at any instant: the duplex stays intact
Compression windows: pairs start opening at 5.5°/bp and always open above 8.7°/bp (Curuksu: 8.6–9.3)
So the chimera is not bent enough to kink on this force field
The DNA touches the protein in 72–98 % of frames (50 nt ssDNA loop 93 %): local contact, not action at a distance

slides.q: Does adding the tet groups change the protein’s local conformation?

points.text: In the AlphaFold model Asp7 sits in left-handed α (+65, +57), on the floppy N-tail (pLDDT 52)
Unclicked 2× Tet2-Et flips it to right-handed α: −53, −46
Clicked (+35, +53), ssDNA (+49, +33) and dsDNA (+65, +14) put it back in left-handed α
Asn553 (HEAT 14 helix) stays at −52 to −60, −29 to −46 in every system
Answer: only the tail site moves, and the click restores it

slides.title: PP2A: backbone rigidity (RMSF)
slides.q: Does the spring deform the scaffold? Does the fold stay intact?

items.cap: Cα RMSF aligned on the core, HEAT repeats shaded
Bend and twist per HEAT repeat; horseshoe aperture

points.text: Core RMSF 2.1–2.6 Å for apo, tet, clicked and 50 nt ssDNA; helix fraction ≈ 0.77 throughout
The 50 bp dsDNA run is the outlier: core RMSF 17 Å, RMSD up to 57 Å
HEAT 12 is the most variable repeat; with ssDNA the aperture changes by only +0.8 ± 2.8 Å
Along the spring coordinate κ ≈ 1–2 kBT nm⁻², about 100× softer than sfGFP’s barrel
Answer: a single strand leaves the scaffold intact; a soft horseshoe could feel a few pN

items.cap: Cβ7–Cβ553 against the clicked zero
Bare-strand restraint windows against the models

points.text: Against the clicked zero: ssDNA −3.1 ± 3.5 Å (p = 0.39), dsDNA +8.0 ± 6.8 Å (p = 0.26); neither resolved
The strand sits at 95 Å, its own rms size: Marko–Siggia says it pulls with 1.74 pN
A 50 bp duplex at this span would push 2.0–2.6 pN by Zocchi’s kinked branch
Bare ss50 windows agree with Marko–Siggia within error (−1.23 ± 1.70 pN at 100 Å)
Bare ds50 at 62 Å: +11.2 ± 1.9 pN measured against 0.9 pN modelled, again far above the model

slides.title: PP2A: DNA dynamics
slides.q: Is the DNA kinked or coiled? Does it interact with the protein beyond pulling?

items.cap: Bend, sharp turns, torsions and stacking along each strand
Strand size and modelled tension over time

points.text: ssDNA end-to-end 95 ± 9 Å against a free-chain rms of 94 Å: neither slack nor taut
Sharp (> 90°) backbone turns in 18 % of frames, hottest at nt 3 by the tether: no interior kink
78 % of adjacent bases stay stacked; 15 % of the backbone in BII
3 of 50 nt on the protein at any time, mostly the N-tail (Met1–Asp5, Tet sites, Gln557)
dsDNA bends 4.9°/bp; the 6.3 open base pairs are at the end (bp 50): fraying, not a kink
